title: 28个选区集体转向：民主党优势进入220席，费城独苗成例外
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: It's great to have you back, Kyle, to see almost 30 races moving in the same direction certainly is something.
segments.zh: 凯尔，很高兴你回来，近30个席位朝同一方向移动确实值得关注。

segments.en: Are these unique to each individual seat, or is this just something indicative of a wave happening?
segments.zh: 这些是每个席位独有的情况，还是表明了一种浪潮正在发生？

segments.en: Yeah, it's much more of the forest than the trees. We could talk about the specifics of a lot of these races, but the overall environment is really which is pushing us to make a lot of changes.
segments.zh: 是的，这更像是整体趋势而非个别现象。我们可以讨论许多席位的具体细节，但整体环境才是推动我们做出许多改变的原因。

segments.en: And we've moved a lot of things in our ratings toward the Democrats, House governor and Senate.
segments.zh: 我们在众议院、州长和参议院的评级中，已将许多事项转向有利于民主党的方向。

segments.en: Since Labor Day, I think a lot of us were waiting to see what would happen after the summer and the start of the traditional campaign season.
segments.zh: 自劳动节以来，我想我们很多人都在等待夏季过后以及传统竞选季开始后会发生什么。

segments.en: Start of course, the campaign season goes away before Labor Day these days.
segments.zh: 当然，如今竞选季在劳动节前就开始了。

segments.en: But what we saw at Labor Day was that the president's approval basically still kept getting worse, or staying in a reduced position.
segments.zh: 但我们在劳动节看到的是，总统的支持率基本上仍在承压，或维持在较低水平。

segments.en: And the Democratic lead in House generic ballot polling ticked up a few points, too.
segments.zh: 民主党在众议院通用选票民调中的领先优势也上升了几个百分点。

segments.en: And we just had a couple of prominent ones come out this morning, New York Times.
segments.zh: 今天早上我们刚看到几个 prominent 的民调结果，《纽约时报》的。

segments.en: I think was D plus 10 or 11, CNN was D plus 10.
segments.zh: 我记得是民主党领先10或11个百分点，CNN是民主党领先10个百分点。

segments.en: I mean, those are, that's like what we saw in 2018 or maybe even a little bit better than what we saw in 2018.
segments.zh: 这就像我们在2018年看到的情况，甚至可能略好一些。

segments.en: So I think this is much more just about the overall environment as opposed to race by race developments.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这更多是整体环境的影响，而非逐个选区的变化。

segments.en: I mean, look, there are going to be exceptions to the rules. Like Brian Fitzpatrick, who is the Republican in the Philadelphia area, he might survive
segments.zh: 当然，规则总有例外。比如费城地区的共和党人布莱恩·菲茨帕特里克，他可能保住席位，

segments.en: even though he's one of the few Republicans in a Harris one seat.
segments.zh: 尽管他是哈里斯领先一个百分点的选区中为数不多的共和党人之一。

segments.en: But that's more of the exception than the rule.
segments.zh: 但这更多是例外，而非普遍现象。
